name: Zimbabwean Exemption Permit (ZEP)

requirement_groups.name: Existing ZEP holder, nationality-based renewal only

requirements.blocker_text: Restricted to Zimbabwean nationals who already hold a valid ZEP under the special dispensation regime dating to 2009 (originally the Dispensation of Zimbabwean Permit, reissued as the Zimbabwean Special Dispensation Permit in 2014 and the ZEP in 2017) -- this is a closed renewal-only regime for the existing ZEP-holder population (approximately 178,000 people), not an open first-time application category for new Zimbabwean arrivals.
requirements.fix_path: New Zimbabwean arrivals without an existing ZEP must apply through the mainstream points-based system instead; ZEP is not available as a fresh entry route.

evidence_required.document: Existing, previously-issued ZEP or documented prior Dispensation of Zimbabwean Permit / Zimbabwean Special Dispensation Permit history
Renewal application within the current gazetted extension window

outcome.duration_length: currently valid until 28 May 2027, per an 18-month extension gazetted 7 October 2025 -- the permit's history shows a repeated pattern of last-minute extensions rather than a fixed long-term validity period

sources.title: Pindula -- Zimbabwean Exemption Permit (ZEP): History, Legal Challenges, Extensions, citing the October 2025 18-month extension to 28 May 2027 and the approximately 178,000 current holder population
Fragomen -- South Africa: Zimbabwe Exemption Permit Update, tracking the litigation timeline including the June 2024 Constitutional Court dismissal of the Minister's appeal
Moneyweb -- Back to court for Zimbabwean permit holders seeking to stay in SA, reporting Operation Dudula's 2026 legal challenge to the Minister's own extension decision

notes: STATUS: DRAFT, and the single most legally contested route documented anywhere in this dataset -- a live, multi-year, still-unresolved court battle rather than settled policy. Timeline, confirmed across multiple independent sources: the special dispensation began in 2009 (Dispensation of Zimbabwean Permit), was reissued as the Zimbabwean Special Dispensation Permit in 2014 and the ZEP in 2017; in November 2021 the Minister of Home Affairs announced termination effective 31 December 2022; the Helen Suzman Foundation challenged this, and in June 2023 the Pretoria High Court declared the termination unlawful, unconstitutional, and invalid for failing to follow the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act's fair-process requirements; the Minister's appeal was refused by the Supreme Court of Appeal, and the Constitutional Court itself dismissed a further appeal on 20 June 2024, leaving ZEPs valid pending a proper consultation process; the Minister then extended validity multiple times, most recently by 18 months (to 28 May 2027) via a gazette published 7 October 2025. As of this research pass, a THIRD active legal front has opened: the anti-immigration group Operation Dudula filed a notice of motion in 2026 challenging the Minister's authority to grant that same October 2025 extension, arguing procedural irregularity -- meaning this route's future is genuinely unresolved from multiple directions simultaneously (undocumented status if the extension is struck down going one way; abrupt termination if a future court forces faster consultation-completion going the other). Structurally closer to Brazil's Mercosur route in being a nationality-gated, broad-rights (work/study/business all permitted) status requiring no economic test -- but critically NOT an open, first-time-applicable route the way Mercosur is: ZEP is closed to new Zimbabwean applicants and exists solely to regularise an already-fixed historical population, a fundamentally different shape from Brazil's ongoing, open bloc-nationality mobility agreement. leads_to_pr is correctly false: no source identified a direct ZEP-to-permanent-residence conversion pathway; holders wanting to settle permanently must separately qualify under one of za_permanent_residence's ordinary Section 26/27 categories like any other foreign national, a real structural dead-end given how long many holders have already resided in South Africa (a decade or more for original 2009 arrivals).
